description: Frontend UX refactor: replace the flat app.tsx layout with a navigable shell (collapsible left sidebar: Chat / History / Settings), move heavy config into a Settings area with sub-navigation, extend the routing-mode control to a 4-position segmented toggle wired to the backend routing mode from FEAT-002, and introduce a clean modern dark+light theme via a design-token/CSS-variable system with a system-preference default and a manual toggle in Settings > Appearance (persisted to localStorage). Reuse the existing feature components; do not rewrite their internals beyond nav integration. Keep the SINGLE top-level onCoreEvent subscription intact across view switches. Depends on FEAT-002 (routing-mode command + types) and FEAT-001 (branch).
steps: TYPES/IPC (mirror FEAT-002 backend): in frontend/src/types/index.ts add `export type RoutingMode = "auto" | "preferLocal" | "preferQuality" | "manual";` and add `routingMode: RoutingMode | null;` to the Conversation interface (keep it a single-line-friendly camelCase mirror of the Rust DTO; note serde omits it when None so it may be absent -> treat missing as null/Auto). In frontend/src/ipc/commands.ts add `setConversationRoutingMode(conversationId: string, mode: RoutingMode | null): Promise<Conversation>` invoking "set_conversation_routing_mode" with { conversationId, mode }, mirroring setConversationRoute.

STATE: in frontend/src/state/conversations.ts add a `setConversationRoutingMode(conversationId, mode)` action that calls the new command and updates the cached conversation in the store (same pattern as setConversationRoute). Keep the existing setConversationRoute (used for Manual pins). Update the ConversationsState interface + any test store-reset shapes if they enumerate fields.

ROUTING-MODE CONTROL: extend frontend/src/features/model-selector/RoutingModeToggle.tsx to a 4-position segmented control (role=radiogroup) with radios Auto, Prefer Local, Prefer Quality, Manual. Derive the active position from the conversation: Manual when conversationPref is set OR routingMode === "manual"; otherwise use routingMode (defaulting missing/null to Auto). On selecting Auto/Prefer Local/Prefer Quality: call setConversationRoutingMode with the matching mode AND clear any manual pin via setConversationRoute(id, null) when leaving Manual. On selecting Manual: call setConversationRoutingMode(id, "manual") and reveal the existing ProviderModelPicker to choose the pin via setConversationRoute(id, route) (existing behavior). Keep AutoRationaleTooltip shown for the non-Manual modes. Add a source comment noting a future continuous slider could drive the same modes. Preserve the empty render when activeConversationId is null.

APP SHELL: rewrite frontend/src/app.tsx into a navigable shell. Keep the SINGLE top-level onCoreEvent useEffect exactly as-is (one subscription, fan-out to all stores, stable cleanup) - do NOT create competing subscriptions and ensure it lives at the shell root so view/route switching never tears it down. Add a collapsible left sidebar (aside) hosting the brand/logo (from FEAT-004 logo.svg; until then a placeholder) and primary destinations Chat, History, Settings (role=navigation with buttons/links; a collapse toggle button that toggles a data-collapsed attribute + persists collapse state is acceptable). Main pane renders the active destination: Chat (default) = existing MessageList + RoutingModeToggle + Composer + PermissionPrompt + the model-selector's per-conversation model + routing-mode control near the Composer (RouteBadge already surfaces the chosen provider/model + rationale); History = existing History surface; Settings = the Settings area below. Fold the app-version footer/StatusBar into the shell (keep the app-version data-testid so its test still passes).

SETTINGS SUB-NAV: build a Settings area (e.g. features/settings/Settings.tsx + a SettingsNav) with sub-sections, each rendering an EXISTING surface or control where one exists: 'Providers & Keys' (provider config + set_provider_secret path - reuse the provider/secret UI currently reachable; if provider config lives inside tool-manager or a providers surface, mount that piece here), 'Local Runtimes' (LM Studio / generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints; include a clearly-labeled EMPTY-STATE placeholder area for future Ollama / Hugging Face - do NOT implement them), 'MCP / Tools' (existing ToolManager), 'Agents' (existing AgentEditor / personas), 'Routing' (routing defaults + explanation of the routing modes; the per-conversation routing-mode control itself stays near Chat), 'Appearance' (theme toggle). Use role=navigation / role=region with accessible names so RTL can target them. Reuse existing components; only add thin wrapper/section scaffolding.

THEME SYSTEM: create frontend/src/styles/tokens.css (or theme.css) defining CSS custom properties for colors, spacing, radius, and typography, with a light palette on :root and a dark palette under [data-theme="dark"] (and honoring @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) as the default when no explicit choice is stored). Accent: a modern teal/blue fitting 'harbor'. Create frontend/src/styles/app.css (or similar) implementing the actual layout styling for the shell/sidebar/Chat/Settings/segmented control/route-badge using ONLY these variables (hand-rolled CSS, NO UI-component library). Cover spacing, hover/active states, focus-visible for a11y, empty states, and a responsive sidebar. Import the stylesheet(s) in frontend/src/main.tsx.

THEME TOGGLE + PERSISTENCE: add a small theme module (e.g. frontend/src/state/theme.ts or a hook) that resolves the initial theme from localStorage key (e.g. 'ah-theme') falling back to system preference, applies it by setting data-theme on document.documentElement, and exposes a setter that persists to localStorage. Wire an accessible toggle (light / dark / optionally 'system') into Settings > Appearance. Guard localStorage/matchMedia access for the jsdom test environment (they exist in jsdom but matchMedia may need a test-setup shim - check test-setup.ts and add a matchMedia stub there if missing).

TESTS: update frontend/src/app.test.tsx so it (a) still asserts the app-version renders, (b) asserts the sidebar renders the Chat/History/Settings destinations, (c) asserts switching to History and Settings renders those views while the History region / a Settings region appears, (d) STILL asserts exactly ONE listen() subscription is opened for the whole shell and that switching views does NOT open a second or call unlisten (assert listen called once after navigating between views), (e) keeps the unmount teardown assertion. Add a settings.test.tsx asserting each Settings sub-section renders (by accessible name) including the Local Runtimes empty-state placeholder. Update model-selector.test.tsx for the 4-position RoutingModeToggle: Auto/Prefer Local/Prefer Quality call set_conversation_routing_mode with the right mode (and clear the pin when leaving Manual), Manual reveals the picker and pins via set_conversation_route (preserve the existing two passing assertions' intent). Add a theme test asserting the toggle switches data-theme and persists to localStorage. FOLLOW THE VITEST RULE: any test that mutates a Zustand store outside act() then reads the DOM must use await findBy*/waitFor, never synchronous getBy.

SELF-AUDIT (offline): no unused imports/vars, correct strict TS types (Conversation.routingMode optional handling), react-hooks exhaustive-deps satisfied (the single onCoreEvent effect keeps its [] deps and reads store getState like today), no floating promises (void the fire-and-forget command calls as the existing code does). Keep TS union types single-line when <=100 cols.
FORMAT: from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend run `NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check .` and fix any formatting (semi, double quotes, trailing commas, printWidth 100, LF).
acceptance_criteria: app.tsx renders a collapsible left sidebar with Chat / History / Settings destinations; Chat is the default view and hosts the chat surface + the routing-mode control + RouteBadge.
The onCoreEvent subscription is opened exactly once at the shell root and is NOT torn down or duplicated when switching between Chat/History/Settings (asserted in app.test.tsx).

Settings has sub-navigation rendering Providers & Keys, Local Runtimes (with a labeled empty-state placeholder for future Ollama/HF), MCP / Tools, Agents, Routing, and Appearance, reusing the existing surfaces.

RoutingModeToggle is a 4-position segmented control (Auto / Prefer Local / Prefer Quality / Manual); Auto/Prefer Local/Prefer Quality call set_conversation_routing_mode with auto/preferLocal/preferQuality and clear any pin when leaving Manual; Manual reveals the picker and pins via set_conversation_route.

A design-token CSS-variable system provides dark + light themes with system-preference default and a manual toggle in Settings > Appearance that persists to localStorage; no heavy UI library was added (package.json dependencies unchanged except none).
vitest suites (app, settings, model-selector, theme) are updated/added and follow the act()/findBy rule; `npx prettier --check .` passes.
verification: NODE_OPTIONS= npx prettier --check . exits 0 from hybrid-orchestrator/frontend

Inspection: app.tsx keeps a single onCoreEvent useEffect at the shell root; package.json has no new UI-library dependency; tokens/theme CSS is imported in main.tsx; RoutingModeToggle has 4 radios wired to set_conversation_routing_mode + set_conversation_route.

CI (authoritative): frontend npm install + eslint + prettier format:check + vitest run all pass on ubuntu-latest and windows-latest, including the new/updated shell, settings, routing-mode, and theme tests.
